extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comics fans, and writers/researchers interested in Alan Moore's views on comics and writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for writing and judging comic-book scripts and narratives, as articulated through Alan Moore's interviews, self-critiques, and commentary. Emphasizes craft (plot structure, dialogue, pacing), originality, use of symbolism, and the affordances of the comics medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator-owned material should not mimic mainstream comics
rubrics_metrics.description: "With a very few bold exceptions, most of the creator-owned material produced by the independent companies has been indistinguishable from the mainstream product that preceded it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creator-owned work should strive to be distinct and original rather than merely replicating mainstream commercial formulas; seek boldness and difference rather than rehashing established tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overuse of elliptical 'bookend' plot structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore criticises his own overuse of "a basic elliptical plot structure, where elements at the beginning of the story mirror events which are to happen at the end ... acting as bookends to give the story that takes place in between a sense of neatness and unity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While mirroring can provide unity and neatness, overreliance on this device is a fault—use it judiciously to avoid predictability or structural laziness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive overlapping or coincidental dialogue in transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: He has also faulted his own excessive use of overlapping or coincidental dialogue in scene transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scene transitions should feel organic; avoid contrived or repetitive overlapping dialogue used merely to stitch scenes together, which can feel like an artifice rather than a smooth flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit comics' affordance of precise textual control
rubrics_metrics.description: "In comics, I have complete control, other than the input of my artists... every full stop and comma that I put down on that script is going to end up in the finished comic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that comics permit precise control over text and pacing; writers can and should craft scripts with attention to punctuation, line breaks, and word placement because these choices will strongly affect the final work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use minimal dialogue in action/fight scenes to preserve visual pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore complimented Frank Miller's realistic use of minimal dialogue in fight scenes, which "move very fast, flowing from image to image with the speed of a real-life conflict, unimpeded by the reader having to stop to read a lot of accompanying text."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let images carry action-heavy sequences; keep dialogue spare so the visual flow remains fast and kinetic—text that interrupts the images can slow down perceived motion and reduce realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing/art should manipulate symbols to change consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: "I believe that magic is art, and that art... is literally magic. Art is, like magic, the science of manipulating symbols, words or images, to achieve changes in consciousness... to cast a spell is simply to spell, to manipulate words, to change people's consciousness"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat storytelling and symbolic choices as tools for affecting readers' perceptions and states of mind; deliberate symbolic manipulation (language, imagery, motifs) is a valid and powerful artistic aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ symbolism, foreshadowing, sophisticated plotting, and mature themes to elevate comics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Filled with symbolism, foreshadowing, and ahead-of-its-time characterization thanks to adult themes and sophisticated plotting, Watchmen elevated the superhero comic book into the realms of true modern literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To lift comics beyond mere genre entertainment, incorporate layered symbolism, foreshadowing, complex characterization, mature thematic content, and carefully structured plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the dearth of new ideas in superhero comics—prioritize originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore criticized "the dearth of new ideas in modern superhero comics" and accused some contemporary work of reusing or ripping off prior concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for genuinely new concepts and perspectives rather than re-treading earlier stories or appropriating prior material; originality is a key evaluative metric in contemporary comics writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symbolic/esoteric systems as tools for idea-generation and narrative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore conceptualised an 'Idea Space' and believed that to navigate this space, magical systems like the tarot and the Qabalah would have to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider employing structured symbolic systems (e.g., tarot, Qabalah) as generative or organizational tools for themes, character archetypes, and narrative architecture—especially if seeking mythic or esoteric resonance.
